scope: Extend whole-operation ASCII and Binary DXF allocation-failure coverage from the rich BLOCK_RECORD route to every public writeBlockRecord overload across eligible revisions, including a caller-populated BLOCK/ENDBLK definition envelope, preserving caller fields and checking typed readback.

source.profile: Generated drawings with one named BLOCK_RECORD, a matching BLOCK/ENDBLK envelope, two INSERTs and a caller-populated ENDBLK footer across AC1014, AC1015, AC1018, AC1021, AC1024, AC1027 and AC1032. The block has a nondefault base point and description. Four writer routes are exercised: (1) name and insertion units, (2) name, units, and preview bytes, (3) name, units, preview bytes, and ordered INSERT source handles, and (4) the same plus APPID/XDATA. The handle-bearing routes begin at AC1015 because the writer refuses BLKREFS at AC1014. Footer readback selects the generated footer among canonical model/paper-space footers and verifies caller fields, structural handle, versioned BLOCK_RECORD owner, lineweight emission boundary and transparency emission boundary. Fields omitted or version-gated by a route are checked against emitted behavior; supplied references are checked against emitted INSERT identities.

implementation.change: Parameterized the focused BLOCK_RECORD whole-operation allocation sweep to invoke all four public overloads across seven supported revisions where each route is admitted, and write a matching BLOCK begin plus caller-populated ENDBLK footer. Fresh readback checks the block name, handle, base point and description; BLOCK_RECORD name, version-available insertion units, optional preview data, optional ordered/remapped INSERT handles and optional APPID/XDATA; and the generated footer's layer, linetype, color, visibility, scale, lineweight, transparency, exact BLOCK_RECORD-handle-plus-two identity and versioned owner pointer. The expectations exercise lineweight serialization from AC1015 and transparency from AC1018; preceding targets retain defaults. Caller preservation, identity rollback, stage cleanup, and retry checks apply to every eligible variant.
implementation.method: For each eligible overload/revision and each ASCII/Binary encoding, calibrate allocation count from a successful clean export, inject std::bad_alloc at every reached offset with a prior destination sentinel, require failure and exact destination/source preservation plus identity-ledger rollback and stage cleanup, then retry the same codec and require byte-identical output and fresh typed readback.

validation.focusedCTest: cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dxf_write_allocation_transaction_tests -j4: PASS; ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_dxf_block_record_allocation_transaction$' -V: PASS 1/1 in 15.00 seconds
validation.result: All 52 eligible revision/overload/encoding combinations passed rollback, same-codec retry, byte-identical output, caller preservation, stage cleanup, and typed BLOCK/BLOCK_RECORD/ENDBLK/INSERT readback. The custom footer's structural identity equals its BLOCK_RECORD handle plus two; its owner pointer follows the AC1015 boundary. Footer fields preserve the supplied layer, linetype, color, visibility and scale. Lineweight uses the supplied width09 from AC1015; transparency uses the supplied explicit alpha 0x40 from AC1018. Earlier revisions read back their documented defaults. BLKREFS overloads are not invoked at AC1014; insertion-units readback is version-gated until AC1021.

limitations: Generated output transaction and typed readback evidence only; no producer-authored preview semantics, broad BLOCK_RECORD graph closure, or native consumer claim follows.

The version matrix uses locally generated drawings. Producer-authored semantics, independent interoperability, complete reference closure, and native consumer behavior remain separate qualification work.
